summary.short: Proposes a federal intellectual property right in an individual's voice and visual likeness, enforceable through civil action against unauthorized digital replicas and products designed to produce them, with notice-and-takedown safe harbors for online services; applies from 180 days after enactment.
summary.long: The bill would create a federal right to authorize use of an individual's voice or visual likeness in a digital replica (a highly realistic computer-generated representation of that individual) or in a product or service requiring such authorization. The right is licensable, not assignable during life, and survives death for 10 years, extendable in 5-year periods on active authorized use, ending no later than 70 years after death. Lifetime licences last up to 10 years and must be written, signed and specific; licences involving minors last up to 5 years, end at age 18 and require court approval. Liability attaches to unauthorized digital replicas made available to the public and to products or services primarily designed to produce them. Online services with a designated agent, a repeat-violator policy and prompt removal after compliant notice are shielded for user-uploaded material. Knowingly false notices incur liability of the greater of $25,000 per notification or actual damages. Civil actions allow statutory damages (individuals: $5,000 per work), injunctions and a three-year limitations period. Exceptions include news, documentary, commentary and parody uses. State-law claims are preempted, except those existing on 2 January 2025. Liability covers only post-enactment conduct; the Act takes effect 180 days after enactment.

relations.target_text: State-law causes of action for protection of an individual's voice and visual likeness rights in connection with a digital replica in an expressive work
relations.note: Preemption is subject to the savings clause in Sec. 2(g)(2), which excludes state causes of action existing as of January 2, 2025, and certain state statutes on sexually explicit or election-related digital replicas, and on products capable of producing digital replicas.

evidence.quote: shall preempt any cause of action under State law

notes: The bill does not amend, repeal, or implement any existing instrument, and it states no legal basis. Its only external citations are to Title 17, 47 U.S.C. 230(e)(2) and 18 U.S.C. 2256(2)(A); none is in the registry, so target_instrument_id is left empty (schema requires a string). Sec. 2(g)(2) fixes a reference date of January 2, 2025 for existing state causes of action, which precedes the bill's introduction on April 9, 2025. Sec. 2(g)(1) preempts 'any cause of action', while Sec. 2(g)(2) carves out several categories; these are read together, not as a conflict. The relations section is populated, so the section_status entry below is a schema formality and does not indicate absence of relations.
